sources.citation: Laycock, Donald C. 1975. The Torricelli Phylum. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea Area Languages and Language Study, Vol. 1 (Pacific Linguistics C-38), 767-780. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Phylum-level phonology paragraph (p. 769) covers only segments: 'three positions of articulation; usually no voicing contrast in consonant phonemes; five to eight vowels... fairly high proportion of fricative consonants', with Olo examples. Gnau is mentioned only for tense marking in verbs (p. 772) and in the speaker table (p. 773, 980 speakers). No word on stress or accent for Gnau or for any Torricelli language.
